texts: good. the keepers, the threads, the source lanterns and all three time cues (day 631, Year 2, dawn) are carried, and 'together' correctly keeps this as one joint act rather than splitting it into a separate collecting per keeper.
good. Hesper, the boiling, the threads as what is changed and the sea-water as where it happens are all covered, and the threads are recognised as the same ones collected in the previous sentence.

good. the mire-essence gets its own referent so the later sentences can point back at it, the cauldrons are recorded as where it formed, and 'by evening' is read as a deadline rather than as a point in time.
good. Hesper, the mire-essence and the three clay vessels are all there, with the count of three sitting on the vessels.

good. 'the stored mire-essence' resolves to the essence Hesper put away, and the drawing is recorded both for the keepers as a body and per keeper - which works here because the essence is one single stock.

mixed: the group-level lighting is right, but the per-keeper rule that a plain plural subject drags along copies the whole lantern group into each keeper's share, so the parse ends up claiming every keeper lit every lantern instead of that the keepers between them lit them. Use the same marker you already used in the first sentence: 'The keepers of the East Row together lit the lanterns of the East Row with the stored mire-essence at sundown.'
good. the forty are carried as a counted subset of the fallen feathers rather than as a claim about feathers at large, and the base of the cliff, the morning and Tessa Brae are all covered.
good. 'the feathers' resolves to the forty she collected, and the feather bin is recorded as where they went.
good. a fresh batch of feathers is taken from the same bin, with Bevin Coombe as the taker and the bin as the source.
good. the grinding attaches to exactly the feathers Bevin Coombe took, which is what the following sentences need.
good. it parses as an agentless lighting of the named lantern - no lighter is invented, which matches what the sentence says.

mixed: the scattering itself is fine, but 'the ground feathers' puts 'ground' on the batch as a single object rather than on each feather, which is the reading our plural handling bars. The previous sentence already says Bevin Coombe ground them, so just drop the modifier: 'Bevin Coombe scattered the feathers around the Stilllight Lantern at sundown.' The same shortening works for the next sentence.
good. the warding is carried with the feathers as what wards, the lantern as what is warded, and wraiths as what it is warded against.
good. parses as a fireable blanket denial - no wraith at all has an approach that night - with the quantifier word itself kept on the record.
